sentences.text: The name Lagosuchus translates to 'rabbit crocodile' in Greek.
Fossils of this animal are known from very incomplete remains, including only one hind limb, a scapula, and vertebrae.
The tibia and fibula were narrow and approximately 10% longer than the femur.
Gregory S. Paul inferred that Lagosuchus was one of the smallest Triassic archosaurs, weighing about 167 grams and similar in size to a weasel or ferret.
Thomas Holtz estimated that Lagosuchus could have reached a total length of 1.7 feet and weighed between 50 and 500 grams, similar to a pigeon.
It likely possessed short forelimbs, long shin bones, and a narrow stance, making it an agile biped adapted for running.
Features and comparisons with close relatives suggest it could run on its hind legs for brief periods but likely walked on four legs most of the time.
Lagosuchus was probably an agile predator that could use its speed to chase prey and escape from much larger predators.
It is believed that Lagosuchus and Marasuchus were transitional forms between cold-blooded reptiles and warm-blooded dinosaurs.
Lagosuchus is generally considered closely related to dinosaurs as a member of the group Dinosauromorpha.
In 1975, Jose Bonaparte considered Lagosuchus to be intermediate between pseudosuchians and saurischian dinosaurs.
In 1994, Paul Sereno and Andrea Arcucci reclassified Lagosuchus lilloensis as a new genus, Marasuchus, due to the fragmentary nature of the original type species.
Federico Agnolin and Martin Ezcurra redescribed the holotype skeleton of Lagosuchus talampayensis in 2019.
The estimated time range for Lagosuchus spans from 241.464 to 237 million years ago.
Some paleontologists argue that Lagosuchus is a valid genus and that Marasuchus is a junior synonym of it.
The age of the Chañares Formation has been the subject of much debate.
